# AGENTS.md

Keep this file up to date.

This is knowledge for developing **the slopball client module itself**. It is
*not* the agent contract slopball installs into a session (that is generated by
the binary this repo builds, and lives in `contracts/`).

## What this repo is, and what it is not

`github.com/nwylynko/slopball-cli` is the **public** half of slopball: the source
of the binary a teammate installs and runs. The rule the split follows is one
line — **code that runs on another person's device is public; everything else is
private** — so what is here is exactly the closure of `cmd/slopball`, plus the
release channel that ships it and the guards that police its wire.

What is **not** here, and is not missing:

| | Where it lives |
|---|---|
| The control plane, relay and telemetry **services** | the private services repo |
| The Cloudflare workers, the deploy, the dashboard | the private services repo |
| **Almost every test** — anything needing a database, a control plane, or a credential | the private services repo, as external test packages importing this module |
| The architecture docs, the plans, the ADRs | the private services repo |

**This repo is `source-available`, not "develop here".** Outside contributions
are second-class by construction: the real suite is somewhere you cannot run it.
Issues and PRs are open and welcome — PR CI proves the release matrix builds,
and real validation happens privately before a merge, which is a round trip and
therefore slow. That is a known, accepted cost, not an oversight.

## The one rule about tests here

**A test in this repo may not import anything outside this module.**

Held mechanically by `internal/repoguard`. It is the whole boundary: "no tests
are public" was always shorthand for "nothing that needs a database, a
credential, or the private control-plane harness", and this is the mechanical
version of that sentence. What passes it, and is here:

- `scripts/installer_test.go` — the three-way agreement between `install.sh`'s
  `uname` mapping, the Makefile's `PLATFORMS`, and the release workflow's asset
  names. Break one and an install 404s; nothing else would notice.
- `scripts/updatescript_test.go` — the same for `update.sh`.
- `internal/wiresnapshot`, `internal/wirechanges`, `internal/nextversion` — the
  wire tripwire, the ledger parser, the release derivation. See below.

If a test you want to write needs more than that, it belongs in the private repo
beside the harness that serves it.

## The wire, the ledger, and the release number

Everything a release number *means* is derived here, because the shapes it orders
have their source here.

- **`internal/wiresnapshot/wire-surface.txt`** pins the shapes an
  already-installed slopball can see: the control-plane HTTP types and string
  vocabulary, the session-network framing, the telemetry envelope, the relay
  ticket's claims. Drift is red, and the failure text is the instruction.
  Regenerate with `make wire-snapshot` — only ever as part of a deliberate change.
- **`.wire-changes/`** is the pending ledger: one file per change, one class, one
  sentence written from an *old client's* point of view. Its
  [`README.md`](./.wire-changes/README.md) is the format **and** the
  expand/contract playbook. Read the playbook before writing a `breaking` entry.
- **`make next-version`** derives the next tag from the pending classes and
  prints the changelog verbatim; `make next-version-consume` folds the sentences
  into `CHANGELOG.md` and empties the folder. The tool prints — Nick tags.

Two things live across the repo line and are easy to trip over:

- **The control plane's ROUTE TABLE is not snapshotted here.** It is service
  code. The private repo keeps a routes-only golden beside the mux that
  dispatches it, so a route added or dropped is red *there*.
- **A `breaking` entry's floor is not enforced here.** `ClientVersionFloor` is
  the deployed control plane's property and lives privately. That repo pairs it
  against this repo's `CHANGELOG.md` when it bumps its
  `require github.com/nwylynko/slopball-cli` pin. Which means a `breaking` entry
  here is **not deployable on its own** — it is tagged, then pinned, then the
  floor moves to meet it.

`CHANGELOG.md` prints a breaking bullet as `- floor vX.Y.Z — <sentence>`. That
`floor ` prefix is a **cross-repo contract**, not formatting: the private repo
parses it. `nextversion.FloorPrefix` is the definition, and a guard over there
reads that literal out of this module's source to check the two agree.

## ⚠️ A tag is permanent. Cut it AFTER validation, never as its trigger

`proxy.golang.org` is a pull-through cache, not a registry you publish to. The
first time anything with default Go env resolves
`github.com/nwylynko/slopball-cli@vX.Y.Z`, it fetches that tag, stores the zip
**permanently**, and writes its hash into `sum.golang.org`'s append-only log.
Moving the tag afterwards does not change what the proxy serves, and a direct
fetch gets `checksum mismatch: SECURITY ERROR` that nobody can clear.

So a failed validation on a tagged commit burns the number forever: the
changelog grows a hole and a `retract` lives in `go.mod` for good.

**The order is: private `make test` green on this commit → then tag.** Not the
other way round. `make test` here is a build, a vet and the guard set — it is
green on trees the product does not work on, and it is not the gate.

The same tag fires both workflows, so the CLI release and the box image are one
release rather than two things that can drift. **Publishing is gated on a GitHub
environment approval** — a tag build produces the binaries and the image and then
waits for a human. Fix-forward is for code, not for artifacts strangers install.

## Layout

Feature verticals, flat, no `internal/` for anything a client links — the private
services repo imports these packages, and Go's `internal/` rule is per-module, so
**every package at the top level is exported API of a public module**. Adding one
widens that API on purpose.

`internal/` here is for repo tooling only: things nothing outside this module
imports and no binary links — the wire guards and the release derivation.

- `cmd/slopball` — the binary. Its closure *is* this module.
- `cli` — the cobra tree. `git` — the bundled git and the only shell-out path.
- `session`, `canonical`, `gitserver`, `syncengine`, `cutover` — the repo layer.
- `controlplane` — the client half of the control-plane wire (no database driver,
  ever; the private repo has a guard that fails a `pgx` in this `go.mod`).
- `sessionnet`, `relayticket` — the session network and its tickets.
- `box`, `cloudbox`-facing seams, `migrate`, `placement`, `trust` — hosts and boxes.
- `scripts/` — `install.sh`, `update.sh`, `fetch-bundled-git.sh`, and their guards.

## Build

```sh
make build          # dist/slopball-<os>-<arch> for this machine
make release        # the four-platform matrix the release uploads
make test           # build + vet + the guard set (NOT the product suite)
make wire-snapshot  # regenerate the wire golden, as part of a deliberate change
make next-version   # derive the next tag from the ledger; writes nothing
```

`make fetch-git` downloads the pinned static git distribution into `git/bundled/`
so `//go:embed` can bake it in. It is a prerequisite of everything: without it
the build fails with `pattern bundled/linux-amd64.tar.xz: no matching files
found`. The archives are gitignored and checksum-pinned in
`scripts/fetch-bundled-git.sh` — bump `git/version.go` in lockstep.

`CONTROL_URL` stamps the default control plane at link time. It is empty here on
purpose: a clean checkout has no deployment to name, so a local build keeps its
loopback default. CI passes it from a repository variable. **Never name a
deployment hostname in this repo, not even in a comment** — they were rotated
once and every hardcoded copy went on printing an address that no longer
resolved.
